title: Kernel selector v2 — benchmark results rollup (internal)
content:
Doc intent
- Internal rollup of benchmark-lab runs comparing selector v1 vs v2.
- Audience: Runtime + SRE + Release Eng (for rollout readiness).
- This is not customer-facing; numbers are from Redwood lab workloads.

Definitions / notes
- “prefill” = prompt processing (context ingestion). “decode” = generation token loop.
- seq bucket = selector bucket derived from effective context at time of kernel choice (scheduler signal).
- All deltas reported as v2 vs v1 (negative latency = improvement).
- Throughput is measured at steady-state for the run’s concurrency level.
- Cost/token proxy = GPU_ms_per_token (lower is better); not direct $.

Run metadata
- Runtime builds:
  - v1 selector baseline: runtime-1.18.6 (selector_v1)
  - v2 selector candidate: runtime-1.19.0-rc3 (selector_v2 table-driven registry v1 + seq bucket + gpu normalization)
- Benchmark harness: benchmark-lab @ pr_941_selector_v2_benchmark_matrix
- Perf gate: perf-canary @ pr_388_selector_v2_perf_gate (thresholds listed below)
- GPUs: L4 (24GB), A10 (24GB), A100-80GB, H100-80GB
- Models (representative set):
  - Llama-family: llama-3.1-8b-instruct, llama-3.1-70b-instruct
  - Mistral-family: mistral-7b-instruct-v0.3, mixtral-8x7b-instruct
  - Qwen-family: qwen2.5-7b-instruct, qwen2.5-32b-instruct
- Prompt distributions:
  - Short context: 256–1k tokens
  - Medium context: 2k–4k tokens
  - Long context: 8k–16k tokens
  - Decode lengths: 128 tokens (short gen) and 512 tokens (long gen)
- Concurrency levels (per GPU): 1, 4, 8 (varies by model size; see per-run notes)

Acceptance thresholds (from perf-canary draft)
- p95 end-to-end latency regression must be <= +3% in any “common lane” (Llama/Mistral on L4/A10/A100; short+medium contexts).
- For long-context lanes (>=8k), allow up to +5% if throughput and GPU_ms/token improve >=3%.
- Any correctness issue (NaN/inf, shape mismatch) is a hard stop.

Executive summary (what changed from v1 → v2)
- Overall: v2 is a net win for decode-heavy and mixed workloads, and reduces variance across SKUs by making selection consistent.
- Biggest wins:
  - H100 decode (all families): p95 latency down 6–12%, tok/s up 5–11%.
  - A100 prefill for medium contexts (Llama/Mistral): p95 down 4–8%.
  - L4 short-context mixed workloads: small but consistent p95 down 2–4%.
- Main risk area (pre-fix): A10 long-context prefill regression due to a seq-bucket boundary bug + one suboptimal kernel mapping. Addressed by pr_18571 + registry adjustment.
- Correctness: one kernel choice produced sporadic NaNs for a narrow shape band on A100 in early rc1; blocked, then mitigated by safe-kernel-set fallback + conformance tests (pr_18501) and registry constraint.

Lane-by-lane results (representative lanes)
Lane naming: {model_family}/{phase}/{context_bucket}/{gpu}

1) Llama-family / prefill / short (<=1k)
| GPU  | p50 Δ | p95 Δ | tok/s Δ | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|---------|-------|
| L4   | -1%   | -3%   | +2%     | Stable; selector decisions deterministic after gpu normalization |
| A10  | +0%   | +1%   | +1%     | Essentially neutral; within noise |
| A100 | -4%   | -6%   | +5%     | Better prefill kernel chosen for short regime |
| H100 | -5%   | -9%   | +8%     | Consistent wins |

2) Llama-family / prefill / long (8k–16k)
| GPU  | p50 Δ | p95 Δ | tok/s Δ | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|---------|-------|
| L4   | -2%   | -3%   | +2%     | Slight improvement; watch memory headroom at 16k |
| A10  | +2%   | +6%   | -1%     | REGRESSION in rc2; fixed in rc3 after seq bucket boundary fix + registry tweak (see outliers) |
| A100 | -3%   | -6%   | +4%     | Better long-context kernel mapping |
| H100 | -4%   | -8%   | +6%     | Stable |

3) Mistral-family / decode / medium (2k–4k) + gen=128
| GPU  | p50 Δ | p95 Δ | tok/s Δ | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|---------|-------|
| L4   | -2%   | -4%   | +3%     | Main win is reduced tail variance (kernel choice uniform across runs) |
| A10  | -1%   | -2%   | +2%     | Small win |
| A100 | -4%   | -7%   | +5%     | Bigger win at higher concurrency |
| H100 | -7%   | -12%  | +10%    | Large decode improvement |

4) Qwen-family / mixed (prefill+decode) / medium + gen=512
| GPU  | p50 Δ | p95 Δ | tok/s Δ | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|---------|-------|
| L4   | -1%   | -2%   | +2%     | Registry entry added late (pr_18533) — re-run once merged to main |
| A10  | +0%   | +1%   | +1%     | Neutral |
| A100 | -2%   | -4%   | +3%     | Moderate win |
| H100 | -6%   | -10%  | +9%     | Strong win |

Perf-canary summary (CI-style gates)
- Gate status by date:
  - 2026-02-03: FAIL (A10 long-context p95 +8–11% in Llama prefill lane)
  - 2026-02-06: FAIL (sporadic NaN in A100 conformance lane; blocked rollout)
  - 2026-02-11: PASS after fixes (seq bucket boundary + safe-kernel constraints + conformance suite expanded)
- Canary dashboards referenced in Slack threads:
  - eng-runtime thread_1737398821_900114 (A10 long-context regression triage)
  - incidents thread_1737609012_880010 (transient latency spike during canary enablement)

Outliers / anomalies (important)

A) A10 long-context prefill p95 regression (rc2)
- Symptoms:
  - Lane: llama-3.1-70b / prefill / long (8k–16k) / A10
  - Observed: p95 +8–11%, tok/s -1–3%
  - Only triggers at context lengths near bucket boundary (8k-ish) and higher concurrency.
- Root cause (suspected → validated):
  1) Seq bucket boundary off-by-one misclassified some 8192-token prompts into “medium” bucket, selecting a kernel better for medium but worse for long on A10.
  2) A10 mapping for that bucket was tuned on an older prompt mix (more 4k than 8k), so mis-bucketing amplified the effect.
- Fixes:
  - pr_18571_fix_seq_bucket_off_by_one (bucket boundary)
  - Registry patch in rc3: tightened “long” lane rule to include >= 8192 exactly.
- Current status:
  - Re-run after fix: p95 now +0–2% (within noise) and GPU_ms/token improves ~2%.
- Follow-up:
  - Add a dedicated “boundary” microbenchmark (8190–8200) to perf suite to prevent recurrence.

B) Sporadic NaNs in early v2 canary (A100)
- Symptoms:
  - Rare NaNs in output logits for a specific kernel choice under a narrow shape band.
  - Correlated with a particular attention kernel id in the registry when using grouped-query attention + certain head dims.
- Mitigation:
  - Safe-kernel-set fallback and conformance tests added (pr_18501).
  - Selector v2 now rejects that kernel for impacted (model_family, head_dim, gqa=true) combinations and falls back to known-good kernel.
- Current status:
  - No NaNs observed in conformance suite after rc3 (3 consecutive sweeps).
- Risk note:
  - Still want longer soak in canary because “rare NaN” class can be low-frequency.

C) “Unknown model family” crash in one benchmark lane
- Symptoms:
  - One experimental model metadata record lacked family mapping and triggered a nil-path in selector v2 during registry lookup.
- Fix:
  - pr_18526_fix_unknown_model_family_fallback_bug — unknown families default to safe kernel set + deterministic ordering.
- Current status:
  - Benchmark harness now includes an “unknown family” lane to assert no crash and stable kernel_choice.

D) Telemetry cardinality blow-up (not a perf issue, but impacts observability)
- Observed:
  - kernel_choice labels included raw model_id and raw seq_len, causing high cardinality in early runs.
- Fix:
  - pr_18519_reduce_metric_cardinality_for_kernel_choice — bucketed seq_len, normalized model_family, sampled event logs.
- Current status:
  - Metrics volume reduced ~70% in lab; SRE review pending for production dashboards.

Notes on variance and “why it looks better”
- The “variance reduction” benefit shows up more clearly in p95 than in p50.
- v1 heuristic sometimes chose different kernels across runs due to subtle differences in detected GPU string / metadata completeness.
- v2 selection stabilizes the decision inputs:
  - GPU normalization (A10 vs “A10G” strings, MIG/partitioned reporting)
  - Table-driven mapping keyed on model_family + seq_bucket + gpu_class
  - Deterministic tie-breaking

Action items (owner / due)
- Add boundary microbenchmark for seq bucket edges (8192/16384): Marcus Reed / 2026-02-22
- Expand long-context A10 coverage for Mistral + Qwen (currently fewer samples than Llama): Rina Kobayashi / 2026-02-23
- Add 30–60 min canary soak run focused on NaN detection + long decode stability: Sana Farid / 2026-02-24
- Confirm perf-canary thresholds reflect “allowed regressions” policy for long-context lanes: Sahana Iyer + Allison Grant / 2026-02-26

Recommendation for rollout readiness
- If rc3 remains clean for 2 more benchmark sweeps + a canary soak, recommend proceeding with staged enablement:
  - internal canary → 5% hosted (us-east) → 25% hosted → dedicated opt-in
- Keep emergency kill switch documented and tested (override precedence) for first week post-enable.

Appendix A — raw-ish run links (internal identifiers)
- bench-lab run ids (selected):
  - bl-2026-02-02T0312Z (A10 regression repro)
  - bl-2026-02-10T2218Z (rc3 full matrix sweep)
  - bl-2026-02-12T0455Z (post-telemetry-cardinality patch)
- perf-canary runs (selected):
  - pc-388-2026-02-03 (FAIL: A10 long-context)
  - pc-388-2026-02-06 (FAIL: NaN conformance)
  - pc-388-2026-02-11 (PASS)

Appendix B — quick glossary (for non-runtime readers)
- kernel registry: the table mapping (model_family, seq_bucket, gpu) → kernel id (+ constraints).
- safe kernel set: conservative kernels known to be correct across shapes; used for unknown/partial metadata or as a fallback.
- selector_v1: heuristic-based kernel selection.
- selector_v2: table-driven selection + rule fallback + deterministic ordering.
